title: Polar coordinates and standard polar curves
terms: polar coordinates; Cartesian coordinates; negative radius; polar circle; cardioid; polar-to- Cartesian conversion.

exposition.text:
√
2 2
Polar coordinates satisfy x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ. For nonnegative r, r = x + y ; if signed
radii are allowed, (r, θ) and (−r, θ + π) represent the same point. Angles are determined only
modulo 2π, and tan θ = y/x by itself does not identify the quadrant.
Curves r = 2a cos θ and r = 2a sin θ are circles centered at (a, 0) and (0, a), each of radius |a|. A
cardioid has form r = A(1 ± cos θ) or its sine variant, with orientation determined by the sign
and trigonometric function. Before integrating, identify how often an interval traces the curve;
polar representations are not unique and naive angle ranges may double-count.
A cardioid is also the curve traced by a point on a circle rolling without slipping around the
outside of a fixed circle of the same radius. This equal-radius rolling construction produces its
single cusp.

question.text:
Which Cartesian equation describes r = 4 cos θ − 6 sin θ?
2 2 2 2
(A) (x − 2) + (y + 3) = 13 (B) (x − 4) + (y + 6) = 52
2 2 2 2
(C) (x + 2) + (y − 3) = 13 (D) x + y = 4x + 6y
2 2
(E) x + y = 13

solution.text:
2 2 2 2
Multiply by r to get x +y = 4x−6y. Completing squares gives (x−2) +(y+3) = 4+9 = 13.

Which pair of polar coordinates represents the Cartesian point (− 3, 1)?
(A) (−2, π/6) (B) (2, π/6) (C) (−2, −π/6) (D) (2, 7π/6) (E) (−2, 5π/6)

solution.text:
√ √
For r = −2 and θ = −π/6, x = −2( 3/2) = − 3 and y = −2(−1/2) = 1. Negative radius
reverses the ray; the positive-radius representation is (2, 5π/6).

question.text:
A point on a circle rolling externally around an equal circle traces a cardioid. In suitable coordi-
nates its equation is r = 2(1 − cos θ). Which point is farthest from the origin?
(A) (4, 0) (B) (−4, 0) (C) (0, 4) (D) (0, −4) (E) (0, 0)

The curve r cos θ = 2 is best described as
(A) A horizontal line
(B) A parabola
(C) A hyperbola
(D) A circle through the origin
(E) A vertical line

solution.text:
The polar-to-Cartesian identity x = r cos θ gives exactly x = 2, regardless of the polar coor-
dinates used to represent its points.

What is the Cartesian equation of r cos(2θ) = 4?
2 2 2 2 2 2 2
(A) xy = 2 (B) x − y = 16 (C) x + y = 4 (D) x − y = 4 (E) (x − y) = 4

solution.text:
2 2 2 2 2
Since cos 2θ = cos θ − sin θ, multiplication by r gives x − y = 4, a hyperbola.

question.text:
As θ runs from 0 to 2π, how many times does r = 2 cos θ, with signed radii allowed, trace its
circle?
(A) One half (B) Once (C) Twice (D) Three times (E) Four times

solution.text:
2
Cartesian parametrization gives x = 2 cos θ = 1 + cos 2θ and y = 2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ. The
angle 2θ sweeps 4π, tracing the circle twice. A negative radius does not remove the second
traversal; it represents the same points from opposite rays.
